study.name: When mere action versus inaction leads to robust preference change
study.journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
study.citation: Chen, Z., Holland, R. W., Quandt, J., Dijksterhuis, A., & Veling, H. (2019). When mere action versus inaction leads to robust preference change. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 117(4), 721-740. https://doi.org/10.1037/pspa0000158
study.description: Preregistered, seven experiments; materials and data at https://osf.io/zy9w3/.

description: Wanting for candies, rated before go/no-go training: on each trial participants answered "How much do you want to eat this candy?" on a continuous 0-2 slider anchored "Not at all" and "Very much" (from the experiment program, candyChoice.py: visual.RatingScale(low=0, high=2, precision=100)). Pre-training ratings only, at timepoint 1; the retest sessions of Experiments 4-6 did not re-rate the candies. Experiments 3-6 share one set of 60 loose, unpackaged candies photographed on a white plate (Experiment 3's and Experiment 5/6's image files are byte-identical), and the numbering is consistent across experiments: item-mean wanting correlates r = 0.85-0.93 between the four independent samples. The source identifies stimuli only by image number. Names were read from the photographs, the same method used for chenhol7 in this paper, and only candies identifiable with certainty are held: 42 of 60. The other 18 -- 9 where only a sub-type or brand is uncertain and 9 that could not be named -- are withheld rather than given descriptive placeholders; their ratings ship beside this ingest as heldout_unnamed.csv. Where a candy also appears packaged in chenhol1/2 (cherries, cola bottles) the generic name is used here and the brand is not asserted. Experiment 5: fast choices, 10 repetitions, with a retest session. 60 recruited; the paper excluded 3 on go/no-go accuracy, all 60 are retained here. Experiments 5 and 6 were stored in one raw-data folder and partitioned by the authors' own copy.files.R on each subject's training-length flag; that partition was reproduced exactly.
